key_insight: A hierarchical multilevel Monte Carlo neural critic removes the bias–compute bottleneck in average-reward CMDPs, enabling order-optimal primal-dual actor-critic learning with neural function approximation.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical route to safe reinforcement learning controllers that can optimize long-run performance while enforcing long-run constraints without needing the mixing time.
method: Uses a hierarchical MLMC neural critic to debias both trajectory sampling and critic optimization.
Builds a primal-dual Natural Actor-Critic algorithm on top of the estimator.
Achieves tilde{O}(T^{-1/2}) optimality gap and constraint violation with general policy parameterization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees with order-optimal tilde{O}(T^{-1/2}) rates for both reward optimality and constraint satisfaction, including in the unconstrained setting.
watch_item: The method relies on neural tangent kernel-based analysis and hierarchical MLMC design, so practical performance may depend on approximation quality, optimization stability, and implementation complexity.
paper_title: Hierarchical Multilevel Monte Carlo for Order-Optimal Neural Actor-Critic in Average-Reward CMDPs
